clue.text: Writing surface of French king encircled by bar (7)

indicators.note: the king is surrounded by the bar, so K goes inside STOP

blocks.note: to bar is to stop; it opens around K
K = king, as in chess notation

explanation.surface: A French monarch's writing desk, fenced off behind a barrier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'French king' wants to be ROI; in fact 'French' belongs with 'of' to give DE, and the king is plain K.
explanation.definitionFit: The desktop is the flat top of a desk that you write on.

clue.text: Last month for every politician to leave (6)

blocks.note: December is the last month of the year

explanation.surface: Every December an MP heads off for the holidays.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For every' giving A is the sense in 'fifty pence a go'.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym with a military root: to decamp was first an army striking camp and moving off, now any hasty departure.

clue.text: Set about bringing in a completed upholstery item (4,5)

indicators.note: SET brings A inside itself

blocks.note: set, the plain word, opens around A

explanation.surface: An upholsterer is told to get on with finishing a piece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set about' reads as one phrase meaning 'begin'; it has to be split, SET taking A and 'about' giving C.
explanation.definitionFit: A seat cover is a fitted fabric covering for a chair or car seat.

clue.text: What’s helped to split it — an iceberg? (7)

definitions.text: What’s helped to split it — an iceberg?

indicators.note: to help yourself to something is to take a portion of it, so the answer is a helping taken from the words that follow

blocks.note: the answer sits inside splIT IT AN ICeberg, starting at the last letter of split

explanation.surface: A riddle asking what an iceberg managed to break apart.
explanation.walkthrough: Read whole, the clue asks what an iceberg helped to split; the liner broke in two as it sank in 1912. Read as wordplay, the same words hold the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The whole clue reads straight: the Titanic is the thing an iceberg helped to split, since the ship broke apart after striking one.

clue.text: Italian bread counter popular, too much under glass (9)

definitions.note: PANETTONI is plural; 'bread' is a mass noun covering several loaves.

indicators.note: to run counter is to go the opposite way, so IN OTT is turned round
in a down entry, what is under something comes after it

explanation.surface: In an Italian bakery, loaves are piled too high in the glass display counter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Counter' looks like the shop counter; it is the turnaround signal. PANETTONI is the plural of the Christmas bread panettone.
explanation.definitionFit: Panettone is a sweet Italian bread; PANETTONI is its Italian plural.

clue.text: Riot eliminating last American barrow (7)

indicators.note: TUMULT drops its final letter

explanation.surface: A riot clears the last American off a street trader's barrow.
explanation.walkthrough: A barrow here is not a cart but an ancient burial mound.
explanation.definitionFit: A tumulus is a mound of earth over a grave, a barrow.

clue.text: Staff upset, chasing second person in French royal house (5)

indicators.note: in a down entry, upset turns ROD upside down
DOR chases, so follows, TU

explanation.surface: Palace servants are upset by a French courtier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'French royal house' reads as one phrase, suggesting Bourbon; 'in French' belongs to the wordplay and the definition is just 'royal house'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tudors were the English royal house from Henry VII to Elizabeth I.

clue.text: Copying piece of news picked up with microphone around (7)

indicators.note: in a down entry, picked up means lifted, read bottom to top
MIC goes around the turned ITEM

blocks.note: mic is short for microphone; it opens around METI

explanation.surface: A reporter records a news story using a mic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Picked up' in this microphone surface suggests sound; here it only lifts ITEM so it reads METI.
explanation.definitionFit: Mimetic means imitative, copying something.

clue.text: Synthetic source of confusion in constellation (5)

definitions.note: 'Synthetic' stands as a noun here, a synthetic fibre.

indicators.note: a source is where something starts, so the first letter
'in' in its sense of 'located within', so C is placed within LYRA

blocks.note: Lyra, the Lyre, is a constellation; it opens around C

explanation.surface: An astronomer is muddled by something odd in the night sky.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is an adjective used as a noun: a synthetic is an artificial fibre.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by category: Lycra is the trade name for spandex, a man-made elastic fibre.

clue.text: Leading performer remains for classic song (8)

explanation.surface: A star's ashes are kept to accompany an old song.
explanation.walkthrough: Stardust is the Hoagy Carmichael standard, one of the most recorded songs of the twentieth century.
explanation.definitionFit: Stardust is a 1927 Hoagy Carmichael song, a classic of the American songbook.

clue.text: Humbled Conservative had a career? (9)

blocks.note: to career is to rush headlong, so 'careered' = hastened

explanation.surface: A Tory politician, brought low, looks back on a working life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Had a career' reads as 'worked in a profession'; career as a verb means to rush, and the question mark flags the stretch.
explanation.definitionFit: Chastened means humbled, made less proud.

clue.text: Fellow, running short, is after instant coffee (5)

indicators.note: CHAP comes up short, losing its last letter
the shortened CHA comes after MO

explanation.surface: A man in a hurry grabs instant coffee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Instant coffee' is a single thing in the surface; the two words must be split, 'instant' giving MO.
explanation.definitionFit: Mocha is a type of coffee, originally from the Yemeni port.

clue.text: A bit of cork in my French wine (5)

indicators.note: a bit of cork is just its first letter
'in' in its sense of 'located within', so A and C are placed within MON

blocks.note: mon = 'my' in French; it opens around AC

explanation.surface: A crumb of cork has fallen into a glass of French wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'French wine' reads as the definition; 'French' belongs with 'my' to give MON.
explanation.definitionFit: Mâcon is a Burgundy wine from around the town of that name.

clue.text: Indication of future performer turning in late, finishing early (5,4)

indicators.note: ACTOR turns round to ROTCA
'in' in its sense of 'located within', so ROTCA is placed within TARD
TARDY finishes one letter early, losing Y

blocks.note: TARDY minus its last letter; it opens around ROTCA

explanation.surface: A future star turns up late to rehearsal and leaves early.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Future performer' reads as a rising star; the definition stops at 'future', and 'performer' starts the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Tarot cards are used in fortune-telling to indicate what lies ahead.

clue.text: Two London termini denied King’s top award (8,5)

indicators.note: KING'S CROSS is denied KING'S, leaving CROSS

blocks.note: Victoria is a London mainline terminus
the second terminus, King's Cross, without King's

explanation.surface: A traveller stranded between two London stations misses a royal honour.
explanation.walkthrough: Victoria and King's Cross are both London railway termini. The Victoria Cross is Britain's highest award for gallantry.
explanation.definitionFit: The Victoria Cross is the highest British military award for bravery.

clue.text: Jazz standard trendy with those people — love upcoming party (2,3,4)

indicators.note: in a down entry, coming up means read bottom to top, so DO becomes OD

explanation.surface: Hip people flock to a love-themed party where a jazz classic plays.
explanation.walkthrough: In the Mood is the Glenn Miller swing hit of 1939.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Mood is a swing-era jazz standard made famous by Glenn Miller.

clue.text: Individual upset about hotel employment after work place welcoming everybody (4,5)

indicators.note: in a down entry, upset turns ONE upside down to ENO
'about' in its sense of 'surrounding', so ENO surrounds H
'after' in its sense of 'following in order', so the rest follows OP

blocks.note: one = a single individual; turned, it opens around H
H = hotel in the phonetic alphabet
use = employment, as in 'the employment of force'

explanation.surface: A worker, unhappy about a hotel job, wants a more welcoming workplace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Work place' in the surface looks like 'workplace'; 'work' is OP and 'place welcoming everybody' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An open house is a home or event where all comers are welcome.

clue.text: Big story covering one bit of Earth at intervals (8)

definitions.note: EPISODIC is an adjective; 'at intervals' is an adverbial phrase, used here as a predicate ('it was episodic').

indicators.note: EPIC covers, wraps around, I SOD

blocks.note: an epic is a long heroic tale; it opens around I SOD
a sod is a clod of turf

explanation.surface: A sweeping saga about one patch of ground on Earth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bit of Earth' asks for a first letter; here it is a whole word, SOD.
explanation.definitionFit: Episodic means happening in separate episodes, now and then.

clue.text: Occasional story about bishop — elemental stuff? (8,5)

indicators.note: 'about' in its sense of 'around', so TALE is placed around B

blocks.note: periodic = recurring from time to time
a tale is a story; it opens around B

explanation.surface: A church newsletter runs an occasional piece on the bishop's basic teachings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Elemental stuff' sounds like basics; the question mark flags the pun on chemical elements.
explanation.definitionFit: The periodic table arranges the chemical elements.

clue.text: Eccentric person reduced chances to join dance (7)

indicators.note: ODDS is cut short by its last letter
'to join' in the sense of 'to be attached to', so ODD is attached to BALL

blocks.note: a ball is a formal dance

explanation.surface: An odd character's chances of getting into the dance are slim.
explanation.walkthrough: Odds are chances, as in betting.
explanation.definitionFit: An informal synonym: calling someone an oddball says they behave strangely.

clue.text: Be dismissive of rest of a branch of algebra (7)

blocks.note: to boo is to jeer, dismiss
to lean on something is to rest on it

explanation.surface: Someone dismisses the rest of a mathematics syllabus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rest of' reads as 'the remainder'; 'of' belongs to the definition, which must be adjectival to match BOOLEAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Boolean describes the algebra of true and false devised by George Boole.

clue.text: Encourage operator to release last of numbers (4,2)

indicators.note: SURGEON lets go of a letter
the final letter of numbers, S

explanation.surface: A telephone operator is urged to hang up before the last number.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Operator' suggests telephones; the operator here is a surgeon.
explanation.definitionFit: A phrasal-verb synonym: a crowd urging on a runner is spurring them forward.

clue.text: Bird shelter driving out one dissolute male (9)

indicators.note: the one, I, is driven out of SHIELD

blocks.note: a rake is a dissolute man

explanation.surface: A bird sanctuary evicts a debauched man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bird shelter' reads as one thing; 'Bird' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The shelduck's male is the sheldrake, a large duck.

clue.text: Moved slowly in a jam, losing lead position (5)

indicators.note: WEDGED loses the letter in first position

explanation.surface: A driver crept forward in a traffic jam and dropped from first place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Losing lead position' reads as a race; it removes W, the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To edge is to move slowly and carefully.

clue.text: Expression of surprise about recording considered the most powerful (5)

indicators.note: 'about' in its sense of 'surrounding', so AHA surrounds LP

blocks.note: aha! is a cry of surprise; it opens around LP
an LP is a long-playing record

explanation.surface: A critic gasps at a record hailed as the strongest ever.
explanation.walkthrough: The alpha male of a group is its dominant member.
explanation.definitionFit: Alpha describes the dominant, most powerful member of a group.

clue.text: Alternative difficulty when deposing leader (5)

indicators.note: BOTHER deposes its leader, the first letter

explanation.surface: The trouble with a coup is finding someone else to rule.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deposing leader' suggests a coup; it only removes the B.
explanation.definitionFit: Other means alternative, as in 'the other way'.

clue.text: Opinion backing American Idol (5)

indicators.note: 'backing' in the sense of moving backwards, so AM GOD is read in reverse

blocks.note: an idol is a false god

explanation.surface: A viewer voices support for the television talent show American Idol.
explanation.walkthrough: 'American Idol' is the TV talent show in the surface, and must be split.
explanation.definitionFit: A dogma is a firmly held opinion or doctrine.

clue.text: Try plain writing with a bit of charm? (9)

blocks.note: prose is ordinary writing, not verse
cute = having some charm; the question mark marks the loose fit

explanation.surface: A writer tries to make plain prose a little charming.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Try' looks like 'attempt'; it is the courtroom sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A legal sense: to try a case is to put someone on trial, which is what the prosecution does.

clue.text: Full set of documents returned after church addition to letter (7)

indicators.note: ALL ID comes back, reading DILLA
'after' in its sense of 'following in order', so DILLA follows CE

explanation.surface: A church office sends back a whole batch of papers, with a postscript added to a letter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Letter' reads as correspondence; it is a letter of the alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: A cedilla is the hook added under a letter, as in ç.

clue.text: SF series about to introduce grand prison (7)

indicators.note: DUNE introduces G into itself

blocks.note: Dune, Frank Herbert's science-fiction series; it opens around G
on = about, as in 'a book on birds'

explanation.surface: A science-fiction saga is set to feature a huge prison.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About to introduce' reads as 'soon to introduce'; 'about' is ON and goes at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a dungeon is one particular kind of prison, the dark cell beneath a castle.
